member.name: T:Obsidian.API.Client.EntityRendererProperties
member.summary: How the Obsidian client draws a mod's entity type: a model layer and a texture from the mod's assets, and the keyframed animations it plays. Register it with .

remarks.para: Parts named head turn to where the entity looks, and, without a , parts whose names end in leg swing as it walks (left and right, and front and back, in opposite phases), like vanilla's mobs; other parts stay as modelled unless an animation moves them.

The items the server says the entity holds and wears are drawn on parts named like vanilla's: held items in the hands of right_arm and left_arm, and armour pieces on the parts vanilla's humanoid armour covers (head, body, right_arm, left_arm, right_leg and left_leg), following them. A model without such a part doesn't show what would go on it.

member.name: P:Obsidian.API.Client.EntityRendererProperties.Texture

member.remarks: Only the Obsidian client calls , after the mod's ; servers never do, so a mod whose side is both runs on a server without any client code. Keep client-only work in this method and what it registers.

member.name: M:Obsidian.API.Client.IClientPlugin.ConfigureClient(Obsidian.API.Client.IClientRegistry)
member.summary: Registers the mod's client side. Called when the client loads its mods: at startup, and again on a new instance of the plugin when the player reloads them. What it registers takes effect when it returns, after which takes no more registrations, and is dropped when the mods reload.

member.name: T:Obsidian.API.Client.IClientRegistry
member.summary: What a mod's registers its client side with.

remarks.para: What the mod registers takes effect when returns and stays until the client exits or the player reloads its mods; if it throws, none of it does. The registry is sealed then, since the client loads what depends on it afterwards: registering through it later throws , while stays usable.
Like the server's content, what the mod registers is its own: identifiers are in its namespace (its mod id) and valid by vanilla's rules (lowercase letters, digits and _-./, one :).

member.name: P:Obsidian.API.Client.IClientRegistry.Connection
